findings.statement: For alpha, use an append-only JSONL metadata index with immutable per-run JSON artifacts, a process lock around each single-record append, and readers that reject or ignore an invalid trailing record; keep raw prompts and secrets outside both the index and artifacts.
Alpha history remains small enough that scanning JSONL for exact run-ID lookup and the latest 100 runs has acceptable latency.

All CLI writers on macOS and Linux can honor the same advisory lock and append one complete metadata record while holding it; without that discipline, nearly simultaneous completions can corrupt or interleave the log.
A torn final JSONL record can be detected and ignored or repaired from the immutable run artifact, and losing that final index entry temporarily is acceptable during alpha.

Versioned self-describing JSONL records fit expected alpha schema change and user inspection/export better than requiring immediate relational migrations, while SQLite would provide stronger transactional concurrency and indexed queries.

Migrate the metadata index to SQLite when a representative history benchmark first shows either p95 exact lookup or latest-100 listing above 100 ms, or when lock contention causes any failed or materially delayed append; import JSONL transactionally and retain JSON export.
The 100 ms latency threshold is an alpha operating assumption, not a measured user requirement; representative benchmarks and contention tests have not been provided.

If lock discipline, torn-write recovery, or bounded scan latency cannot be demonstrated, the recommendation changes to SQLite immediately because transactions, uniqueness constraints, and indexes directly address those failures.

alternatives: Use SQLite from alpha with a runs table keyed by run ID, a descending completion-time index, transactional writes, explicit schema migrations, and JSON export; this is preferred if concurrency or recovery assumptions fail.

method_artifact.judgment: Start with lock-protected append-only JSONL metadata plus immutable per-run JSON artifacts; migrate the index to SQLite on the stated latency or contention trigger.
method_artifact.scope: Local macOS/Linux Python 3.12 CLI run metadata only; no implementation and no raw prompt or secret storage.
assumptions: Alpha history remains small enough for acceptable scan latency.
All writers honor one cross-process advisory lock.
A torn final record is detectable and recoverable from immutable run artifacts.
challenges: Lock discipline may fail or differ across target platforms.
A crash may split artifact publication from ledger append.
History growth may make scans too slow.
counterevidence: SQLite provides transactions, uniqueness constraints, and indexes that directly address the challenged JSONL assumptions.
failure_impacts: If lock discipline, torn-write recovery, or bounded scan latency cannot be demonstrated, choose SQLite immediately.
change_conditions: Strengthen the JSONL choice if crash recovery, duplicate handling, and simultaneous-writer tests pass on macOS and Linux.
Adopt SQLite if representative lookup or latest-100 latency exceeds 100 ms, or any append is corrupt, lost, duplicated, or materially delayed by contention.
method_artifact.revised_judgment: Choose SQLite at alpha if any load-bearing JSONL assumption fails validation.

confidence.basis: The recommendation is grounded in the supplied constraints, but no run-count forecast, latency benchmark, crash test, or lock-contention measurement was supplied.

change_conditions: Strengthen the JSONL choice if crash recovery, duplicate run-ID handling, and simultaneous-writer tests pass on macOS and Linux.
Weaken it if history growth makes p95 exact lookup or latest-100 listing exceed 100 ms on representative hardware.
Invalidate it on any observed corrupt, lost, duplicate, or materially lock-delayed append; adopt SQLite with transactional import and JSON export.
